Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front and a proposed next step: a 45-minute walkthrough where we annotate our diagram live.

Summary answers (high level):
- Canonical PII mapping: by default we persist request metadata (timestamps, request IDs), user-provided prompts and completions, minimal user profile fields (email & display name if submitted), and embeddings if a customer opts-in. SAS: we can turn off embeddings persistence.
- Retention: default request/log retention is 90 days; telemetry (metrics/aggregates) retained 365 days. Retention is configurable for Enterprise and Dedicated customers; Private deployments can match your retention SLA.
- KMS: hosted customers can opt into customer-managed keys (CMK) via partner KMS integrations; I'll attach our KMS attestation example and the subprocessor roster.
- Subprocessors: attached CSV includes subprocessors and access type (plaintext, telemetry-only, encrypted-store-only). We surface subprocessors at least quarterly.
- Transfers: we support SCCs in our standard DPA annex and can route EU traffic to EU-hosted capacity; for strict residency we offer Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) as an option.
- Dataflow: attaching an annotated diagram; happy to walk through it.

Next step: can we meet Thursday 28th at 10am PT for a quick walkthrough? If that works, I'll have Connor join to cover KMS and routing.

Thanks,

Alicia — quick technical clarifications to supplement Kim's note below.

- Tokenization / Pseudonymization: For hosted (shared) deployments we strip request-level metadata used for routing; actual prompt/completion text is preserved unless customer requests redaction. We offer tokenization modules that can pseudonymize named entities at ingest — typically deployed on Dedicated or Private.
- KV cache & model runtime: KV cache is ephemeral per session and not materialized to durable storage by default. Backups of model artifacts and checkpoint data do not contain customer prompts.
- KMS & attestation: we can support CMKs via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or GCP KMS. Attached is an example attestation we provide to enterprise customers. For hosted CMK support we can enable key-rotation reporting and exportable audit logs.
- Subprocessor access levels: see attached CSV for explicit "plaintext" vs "telemetry-only" flags. We mark vendors that have cryptographic access (e.g., managed infra) separately.
- Network egress & routing: for EU traffic we route through EU-region clusters when the tenant is flagged. For cross-region failover we provide explicit controls and logs of egress events.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-202704.csv, kms-attestation.txt, egress-routing-diagram.svg
